Here's a regex that matches an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```

- `\d{4}`: four-digit year
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])`: month, 01–12
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])`: day, 01–31
- `\b`: word boundaries, so it won't match inside longer digit strings

It matches `2026-10-01`. It doesn't check that the day exists in that month, so `2026-02-31` also matches. Calendar validity (leap years and so on) needs a date parser, not a regex.

If you need the whole string to be a date, for example when validating input, anchor it instead:

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```
